record.title: Postmortem of database outage of January 31
record.summary: On January 31, 2017, while troubleshooting a broken PostgreSQL replication process on GitLab.com, an engineer intended to wipe the data directory of the secondary database but ran the command against the primary instead, deleting roughly 300GB of production data. This caused a major GitLab.com outage lasting about 18 hours, and because the pg_dump backups had been silently failing and Azure disk snapshots were not enabled for database servers, GitLab had to restore from a 6-hour-old LVM snapshot, permanently losing data created between 17:20 and 00:00 UTC. Recovery required copying data over slow staging disks, taking about 18 hours, before the service and webhooks were fully restored.

document.title: Summary of the Amazon DynamoDB Service Disruption in the Northern Virginia (US-EAST-1) Region

record.title: Summary of the Amazon DynamoDB Service Disruption in the Northern Virginia (US-EAST-1) Region
record.summary: A latent race condition between two independent DynamoDB DNS Enactor processes caused an older DNS plan to overwrite a newer one for the regional DynamoDB endpoint in US-EAST-1, and the subsequent cleanup process deleted all IP addresses for that endpoint, causing widespread DNS resolution failures. This DynamoDB outage cascaded into EC2 instance launch failures (via DWFM lease congestive collapse and Network Manager propagation backlogs), Network Load Balancer health-check failures, and downstream impact to Lambda, ECS/EKS/Fargate, Connect, STS, IAM console sign-in, Redshift, and AWS Support Console, among other services. Engineers manually restored DNS state, throttled and restarted subsystems, and disabled automatic failover mechanisms to recover, with different services fully recovering at different times between roughly 2:40 AM and 2:20 PM PDT on October 20, 2025.

trigger.label: operational_delay
trigger.quote: Right before this event started, one DNS Enactor experienced unusually high delays needing to retry its update on several of the DNS endpoints.
trigger.description: One DNS Enactor experienced unusually high delays retrying endpoint updates while another Enactor rapidly applied a newer plan, activating a latent race condition.

mechanism.label: race_condition
mechanism.quote: the race condition involves an unlikely interaction between two of the DNS Enactors
mechanism.description: A race condition let an older DNS plan overwrite a newer one for DynamoDB's regional endpoint, which was then deleted, removing all its IP addresses.

mitigations.text: Temporary mitigations were applied that enabled some internal services to connect to DynamoDB and repaired key internal tooling.
Manual operator intervention corrected the inconsistent DNS plan state, restoring all DNS information by 2:25 AM.
Engineers throttled incoming work and began selective restarts of DWFM hosts to break the congestive collapse.
Engineers disabled automatic health check failovers for NLB to stop capacity from being incorrectly removed.
Lambda Event Source Mappings and asynchronous invocations were throttled to prioritize synchronous invocations.
Engineers took action to stop the Redshift replacement-workflow backlog from growing further.
Engineers relaxed EC2 request throttles as systems stabilized, working toward full recovery.

blast_radius.qualitative: We know this event impacted many customers in significant ways.

impact_start.quote: the event started at 11:48 PM PDT on October 19

mitigated_at.quote: Customers were able to resolve the DynamoDB endpoint and establish successful connections as cached DNS records expired between 2:25 AM and 2:40 AM. This completed recovery from the primary service disruption event.

remediations.text: Disabled the DynamoDB DNS Planner and DNS Enactor automation worldwide.
Will fix the race condition scenario and add additional protections to prevent application of incorrect DNS plans before re-enabling automation.
Adding a velocity control mechanism to limit capacity an NLB can remove during AZ failover from health check failures.
Building an additional test suite to exercise the DWFM recovery workflow and identify future regressions.

DWFM entered a state of congestive collapse because the large number of droplets meant lease re-establishment work could not complete before timing out again.
NLB health checks failed intermittently because new EC2 instances were brought into service before their network state had fully propagated.

record.title: Summary of the Amazon DynamoDB Service Disruption in the Northern Virginia (US-EAST-1) Region
record.summary: On October 19–20, 2025, a latent race condition in Amazon DynamoDB's automated DNS management system caused an older DNS plan to overwrite a newer one and then be deleted, leaving the regional DynamoDB endpoint with an empty DNS record and causing widespread API errors in US-EAST-1. This DynamoDB failure cascaded into EC2 instance launch failures, Network Load Balancer connection errors, and downstream impact to Lambda, ECS/EKS/Fargate, Amazon Connect, STS, IAM console sign-in, Redshift, and AWS Support Console, among other services. mechanism.quote: The race condition involves an unlikely interaction between two of the DNS Enactors.
mechanism.description: A race condition between two independent DNS Enactor processes caused an older, stale DNS plan to overwrite a newer plan for DynamoDB's regional endpoint, and the subsequent cleanup process deleted that plan, removing all IP addresses for the endpoint and leaving the DNS management system in an inconsistent state that blocked further automated repair.

Manual operator intervention restored DynamoDB's DNS state after the inconsistent state blocked automated updates.
Engineers throttled incoming work and began selective restarts of DWFM hosts to recover from congestive collapse.

record.title: Slack’s Incident on 2-22-22
record.summary: On February 22, 2022, a routine percentage-based rollout of a Consul agent upgrade caused memcached nodes to be sequentially deregistered and replaced with empty cache slots, driving down cache hit rates. Because an inefficient 'scatter query' used to fetch Group Direct Message membership during client boot had to hit every shard on any cache miss, the resulting cache misses overwhelmed the Vitess database. This triggered a cascading failure that caused widespread client boot failures, and Slack mitigated it by throttling boot requests and later fixing the query and cache-refill path.
